links.card_of: Zebadiah: A priest of the family of Immer who had married a foreign wife after the return from exile.

sentences: A priest of the family of Immer, named in the ancestry of priests serving in Jerusalem after the exile.
Meshillemith appears in the ancestry of the priest Maasai, as son of Immer and father of Meshullam (1 Chronicles 9).
links.card_of: Meshillemith: A priest of the family of Immer, named in the ancestry of priests serving in Jerusalem after the exile.

sentences: Returnees from Immer and nearby places could not prove their families belonged to Israel (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's copy of the list records the same returnees from Immer (Nehemiah 7).
links.card_of: Immer: A settlement in Babylonia from which some exiles returned who could not prove their Israelite descent.

options.name: Jabin
options.who: A Canaanite king of Hazor who led the northern kings against Joshua and was killed.

options.name: Jabin
options.who: A king of Canaan reigning in Hazor who oppressed Israel in the days of Deborah.

sentences: Joshua defeats a northern coalition led by Jabin of Hazor and completes the main conquest of Canaan.
Jabin king of Canaan oppresses Israel twenty years through his commander Sisera.
He asks God to treat them as he did Midian, Sisera, and Jabin.
Commander of King Jabin's Canaanite army, defeated by Barak and killed by Jael.
links.card_of: Sisera: Commander of King Jabin's Canaanite army, defeated by Barak and killed by Jael.

sentences: Hivites living under Hermon in the land of Mizpah joined Jabin's northern alliance against Israel (Joshua 11).
links.card_of: Hivites: A Canaanite people descended from Canaan, living at Shechem, Gibeon, and beneath Mount Hermon when Israel entered the land.

sentences: Sisera fled to her tent, since Jabin was at peace with Heber's house (Judges 4).
links.card_of: Jael: The wife of Heber the Kenite, who killed the Canaanite commander Sisera in her tent.

sentences: His household was at peace with Jabin king of Hazor (Judges 4).
links.card_of: Heber: A Kenite, descended from Moses' in-law Hobab, and the husband of Jael, who killed Sisera.

sentences: Jabin king of Hazor led a northern coalition, and Joshua burned the city (Joshua 11).
Later, Jabin king of Canaan reigned in Hazor and oppressed Israel through Sisera (Judges 4).
links.card_of: Hazor: A major Canaanite city north of the Sea of Galilee.

sentences: Jabin king of Hazor summons the king of Achshaph to fight Israel (Joshua 11).
links.card_of: Achshaph: A Canaanite royal city in northern Canaan, later on the border of Asher.

sentences: The psalmist recalls Sisera and Jabin, who perished at En-dor (Psalms 83).
links.card_of: En-dor: A town south of Mount Tabor, best known as the home of the medium Saul consulted.

sentences: The home base of Sisera, commander of the Canaanite king Jabin's army.
Sisera, commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-hagoyim (Judges 4).
links.card_of: Harosheth-hagoyim: The home base of Sisera, commander of the Canaanite king Jabin's army.

sentences: Waters in upper Galilee where Joshua defeated the northern Canaanite kings led by Jabin of Hazor.
Jabin of Hazor and his allies camped together at the waters of Merom to fight Israel (Joshua 11).
links.card_of: Merom: Waters in upper Galilee where Joshua defeated the northern Canaanite kings led by Jabin of Hazor.

options.name: Jacob
options.who: Son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel by God, whose twelve sons became the tribes of Israel.

options.name: Jacob
options.who: Son of Matthan and father of Joseph, Mary's husband, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; not the patriarch.

sentences: The promise passes to Isaac and then to Jacob, whom God renames Israel.
Abraham dies, Ishmael's descendants are listed, and Rebekah bears twins Esau and Jacob, who struggle from birth.
Esau, a hunter, sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew.
Jacob, helped by Rebekah, deceives his blind father Isaac and receives the blessing intended for Esau.
Jacob wears Esau's clothes and goatskins to feel like his hairy brother.
Isaac gives Jacob blessings of abundance and rule over his brothers.
Isaac sends Jacob to Paddan-aram to find a wife, and God appears to Jacob in a dream at Bethel.
Jacob sees a stairway reaching heaven with angels going up and down.
God passes Abraham's promises to Jacob and promises to be with him.
Jacob arrives at Laban's home and works seven years for Rachel, but Laban tricks him into marrying Leah first.
Jacob meets Rachel at a well and is welcomed by Laban.
Jacob marries Rachel a week later in exchange for seven more years of work.
Rivalry between Rachel and Leah produces more sons, Rachel bears Joseph, and Jacob grows rich despite Laban's scheming.
Jacob's breeding methods leave him with the strongest flocks.
Jacob secretly leaves Laban for Canaan, Laban pursues him, and the two make a covenant in Gilead.
God tells Jacob to return home, and Rachel steals her father's household gods.
God warns Laban in a dream not to harm Jacob.
Jacob fearfully prepares to meet Esau, sends gifts ahead, and wrestles with God, who renames him Israel.
Hearing that Esau is coming with four hundred men, Jacob divides his camp and prays.
Jacob wrestles a man all night and will not let go without a blessing.
Esau warmly welcomes Jacob, the brothers reconcile, and Jacob settles near Shechem.
Jacob bows seven times, but Esau runs to embrace him.
Esau accepts Jacob's gifts after Jacob insists.
Jacob's sons deceitfully demand that all the city's men be circumcised.
Jacob rebukes Simeon and Levi for endangering the family.
Jacob returns to Bethel, God reaffirms his name Israel and his promises, and Rachel and Isaac die.
Jacob's household gets rid of foreign gods before going to Bethel.
Jacob's twelve sons are listed, and Esau and Jacob bury Isaac.
Esau moves with his family to the hill country of Seir, away from Jacob.
Jacob favors Joseph, who dreams of ruling his brothers, and the jealous brothers sell him to traders bound for Egypt.
Jacob gives Joseph a richly ornamented robe.
They dip his robe in goat's blood, and Jacob mourns him as dead.
Ten brothers come, but Jacob keeps Benjamin at home.
Their money is secretly returned in their sacks, alarming them and Jacob.
Joseph reveals himself to his brothers, forgives them, and sends for Jacob to come to Egypt.
Jacob is stunned to hear Joseph is alive and resolves to see him.
God reassures Jacob in a vision, and his whole family of seventy moves to Egypt and settles in Goshen.
At Beersheba, God promises to make Jacob a great nation in Egypt.
The chapter lists Jacob's descendants who go to Egypt.
Jacob meets Pharaoh, and Joseph manages the famine so that the Egyptians sell their land and themselves to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh grants the family land in Goshen, and Jacob blesses Pharaoh.
Jacob makes Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan.
Jacob adopts and blesses Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, placing the younger ahead of the older.
Jacob recalls God's promise to him at Luz.
Jacob gives Joseph an extra portion of land.
Jacob speaks prophetic words over each of his twelve sons, then dies.
Jacob asks to be buried at Machpelah with his ancestors.
Joseph buries Jacob in Canaan, reassures his brothers of forgiveness, and dies in Egypt.
Egyptians mourn Jacob, and a great procession goes to Canaan for his burial.
God reveals himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Balaam blesses Israel a third time and foretells a ruler from Jacob who will crush Israel's enemies.
The Lord loves Zion's gates more than all Jacob's dwellings.
He loves justice and has established equity in Jacob.
God chose Jacob as his treasured possession.
The LORD will have compassion on Jacob and settle them in their land.
Jacob's guilt will be atoned when altars and Asherah poles are destroyed.
The deaf will hear, the blind will see, and Jacob will no longer be ashamed.
The coming day is called a time of distress for Jacob.
Jacob is told not to fear, for God will save him.
God brings an indictment against Ephraim and Judah, recalling Jacob's life and Israel's deceit and dishonest trade.
Jacob strove with God and wept, seeking favor, and met God at Bethel.
The vision of Obadiah condemns Edom for violence against its brother Jacob and declares that the kingdom will be the LORD's.
The book ends with confidence in God's pardon and his faithfulness to Abraham and Jacob.
The remnant of Jacob will be like dew among peoples and like a lion among beasts.
God will cast all sins into the sea and show faithfulness to Jacob and Abraham.
God shows his love by choosing Jacob and bringing Edom's land to ruin.
Not all descended from Israel belong to Israel; God chose Isaac and Jacob.
Fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Judah and of King David.
Jacob blessed him, saying the scepter would not depart from Judah (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Judah: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Judah and of King David.

sentences: Favored son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into slavery by his brothers, who rose to rule Egypt.
Jacob's favorite, he dreamed of ruling his brothers, who sold him into slavery (Genesis 37).
He revealed himself to his brothers and brought Jacob's family to Egypt (Genesis 45).
links.card_of: Joseph: Favored son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into slavery by his brothers, who rose to rule Egypt.

sentences: Jacob crossed his hands and blessed Ephraim above his older brother Manasseh (Genesis 48).
links.card_of: Ephraim: Younger son of Joseph born in Egypt, ancestor of the tribe of Ephraim, a leading northern tribe.

sentences: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin.
Dying Rachel named him Ben-oni, 'son of my sorrow,' but Jacob called him Benjamin (Genesis 35).
Rachel died giving birth to him; she named him Ben-oni, but Jacob called him Benjamin (Genesis 35).
links.card_of: Benjamin: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin.

sentences: Older twin brother of Jacob, son of Isaac and Rebekah, and ancestor of the Edomites.
Born first of twins, he later sold his birthright to Jacob for a meal (Genesis 25).
Jacob received Isaac's blessing instead of him, and Esau planned to kill Jacob (Genesis 27).
links.card_of: Esau: Older twin brother of Jacob, son of Isaac and Rebekah, and ancestor of the Edomites.

sentences: The promised son of Abraham and Sarah, father of Jacob and Esau, and heir of God's covenant.
Old and blind, he was deceived into blessing Jacob instead of Esau (Genesis 27).
He died at an old age and was buried by Esau and Jacob (Genesis 35).
links.card_of: Isaac: The promised son of Abraham and Sarah, father of Jacob and Esau, and heir of God's covenant.

sentences: Jacob blessed him but placed his younger brother Ephraim ahead of him (Genesis 48).
links.card_of: Manasseh: Firstborn son of Joseph born in Egypt, ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh.

sentences: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Reuben.
He was born to Leah, the first of Jacob's sons (Genesis 29).
Jacob said he would lose his preeminence because he defiled his father's bed (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Reuben: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Reuben.

sentences: Third son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the Levites, Israel's priestly tribe.
Jacob rebuked Levi and Simeon for their violent anger (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Levi: Third son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the Levites, Israel's priestly tribe.

sentences: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Dan.
Jacob blessed him, saying Dan would judge his people (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Dan: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Dan.

sentences: The king of Egypt in Joseph's day, who made Joseph ruler over Egypt and welcomed Jacob's family.
He gave Jacob's family the land of Goshen, and Jacob blessed him (Genesis 47).
links.card_of: Pharaoh: The king of Egypt in Joseph's day, who made Joseph ruler over Egypt and welcomed Jacob's family.

sentences: Son of Jacob by Leah's servant Zilpah, ancestor of the tribe of Gad.
He went down to Egypt with Jacob and his sons (Genesis 46).
Jacob blessed him, saying raiders would attack him but he would strike back (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Gad: Son of Jacob by Leah's servant Zilpah, ancestor of the tribe of Gad.

sentences: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee.
Jacob blessed him as a doe let loose (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Naphtali: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee.

sentences: Rebekah's brother in Haran, father of Leah and Rachel, and Jacob's uncle and father-in-law.
He gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel, then gave Rachel for seven more years (Genesis 29).
He repeatedly changed Jacob's wages while Jacob's flocks increased (Genesis 30–31).
links.card_of: Laban: Rebekah's brother in Haran, father of Leah and Rachel, and Jacob's uncle and father-in-law.

sentences: Sixth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun.
Jacob blessed him, saying he would dwell at the shore of the sea (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Zebulun: Sixth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun.

sentences: Laban's younger daughter, Jacob's beloved wife, and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
Rachel met Jacob at a well while watering her father's sheep (Genesis 29).
Jacob served Laban seven years for her, but Laban first gave him Leah (Genesis 29).
links.card_of: Rachel: Laban's younger daughter, Jacob's beloved wife, and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

sentences: A son of Jacob by Zilpah, Leah's servant, and ancestor of the tribe of Asher.
Jacob blessed him, saying his food would be rich (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Asher: A son of Jacob by Zilpah, Leah's servant, and ancestor of the tribe of Asher.

sentences: Jacob's second son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Simeon.
Jacob's final words condemned the violent anger of Simeon and Levi (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Simeon: Jacob's second son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Simeon.

sentences: Jacob's fifth son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Issachar.
Jacob likened him to a strong donkey bending to labor (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Issachar: Jacob's fifth son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Issachar.

sentences: Merari went down to Egypt with his father Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Merari: The third son of Levi, whose descendants the Merarites served at the tabernacle.

sentences: Laban's elder daughter, Jacob's first wife, and mother of six of his sons.
Laban gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel on the wedding night (Genesis 29).
Jacob placed Leah and her children ahead of Rachel when meeting Esau (Genesis 33).
links.card_of: Leah: Laban's elder daughter, Jacob's first wife, and mother of six of his sons.

sentences: Kohath went down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Kohath: The second son of Levi and grandfather of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

sentences: Daughter of Bethuel, wife of Isaac, and mother of Esau and Jacob.
She helped Jacob obtain Isaac's blessing in place of Esau (Genesis 27).
She sent Jacob to her brother Laban to escape Esau's anger (Genesis 27).
links.card_of: Rebekah: Daughter of Bethuel, wife of Isaac, and mother of Esau and Jacob.

sentences: Gershon went down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Gershon: The firstborn son of Levi, whose descendants the Gershonites served at the tabernacle.

sentences: He went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Perez: Son of Judah and Tamar, twin of Zerah, and ancestor of King David and Jesus.

sentences: Hivite prince, son of Hamor, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.
Jacob bought land near the city from the sons of Hamor (Genesis 33).
links.card_of: Shechem: Hivite prince, son of Hamor, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.

sentences: A Hivite prince of the land around Shechem and the father of Shechem, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.
Jacob bought a piece of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor for a hundred pieces of money (Genesis 33).
After his son seized Dinah, Hamor proposed intermarriage between his people and Jacob's family (Genesis 34).
links.card_of: Hamor: A Hivite prince of the land around Shechem and the father of Shechem, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.

sentences: He was among the family of Jacob who went down into Egypt (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Hezron: A grandson of Judah through Perez whose descendants included King David and, ultimately, Jesus.

sentences: Jacob asked to be buried in the cave purchased from the Hittites (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Heth: A son of Canaan and ancestor of the Hittites, from whom Abraham bought a burial place.

sentences: He went down to Egypt with the family of Jacob (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Zerah: A son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Perez, and ancestor of the Zerahite clan.

sentences: Rachel's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, who bore him Dan and Naphtali.
Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob, and she bore Dan and Naphtali (Genesis 30).
links.card_of: Bilhah: Rachel's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, who bore him Dan and Naphtali.

sentences: Jacob charged his sons to bury him in the cave in the field of Ephron (Genesis 49).
Jacob's sons buried him in the cave Abraham had bought from Ephron (Genesis 50).
links.card_of: Ephron: A Hittite, son of Zohar, who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah as a family tomb.

sentences: Jacob met shepherds who knew Laban, whom they called the son of Nahor (Genesis 29).
Laban and Jacob swore a covenant before the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor (Genesis 31).
links.card_of: Nahor: Brother of Abraham who settled in Mesopotamia; grandfather of Rebekah and Laban.

sentences: Isaac sent Jacob to Bethuel's house to take a wife from Laban's daughters (Genesis 28).
links.card_of: Bethuel: Son of Nahor and Milcah, nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah and Laban.

sentences: Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite violated Dinah, and Jacob's sons avenged her (Genesis 34).
links.card_of: Hivites: A Canaanite people descended from Canaan, living at Shechem, Gibeon, and beneath Mount Hermon when Israel entered the land.

sentences: Daughter of Jacob and Leah, whose violation by Shechem led her brothers to take violent revenge.
Leah bore her to Jacob after six sons (Genesis 30).
She went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Dinah: Daughter of Jacob and Leah, whose violation by Shechem led her brothers to take violent revenge.

sentences: He went down to Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Shelah: The third son of Judah by the daughter of Shua, and ancestor of the Shelanite clan.

sentences: He is listed among the sons of Benjamin who went to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Bela: The firstborn son of Benjamin and head of the Belaite clan.

sentences: Leah's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, and mother of Gad and Asher.
Leah gave her to Jacob, and she bore Gad and Asher (Genesis 30).
Her sons are listed among the twelve sons of Jacob (Genesis 35).
links.card_of: Zilpah: Leah's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, and mother of Gad and Asher.

sentences: He is listed among Asher's descendants who went to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Heber: A grandson of Asher, son of Beriah, and ancestor of the Heberite clan.

sentences: He went down to Egypt with Jacob's family (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Beriah: A son of Asher and ancestor of the Beriite clan.

sentences: Hezron went down to Egypt with Jacob's family as one of Reuben's sons (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Hezron: A son of Reuben and the founder of the Hezronite clan in the tribe of Reuben.

sentences: Pallu went down to Egypt with Jacob's family as one of Reuben's sons (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Pallu: A son of Reuben, founder of the Palluite clan and ancestor of Dathan and Abiram.

sentences: Her sons are listed among Jacob's descendants born to Joseph in Egypt (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Asenath: An Egyptian woman, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, who became Joseph's wife.

sentences: A descendant of Jacob's son Benjamin, son of Bilhan, listed in his tribe's genealogy.
links.card_of: Benjamin: A descendant of Jacob's son Benjamin, son of Bilhan, listed in his tribe's genealogy.

sentences: A grandson of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family.
He went down to Egypt with Jacob as a son of Beriah, son of Asher (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Malchiel: A grandson of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family.

sentences: He condemns Edom for gloating and violence against its brother Jacob when Jerusalem fell (Obadiah 1).
links.card_of: Obadiah: A prophet whose short book, the shortest in the Old Testament, announces God's judgment on Edom.

sentences: A daughter of Asher and granddaughter of Jacob, one of the few women named in Israel's genealogies.
Serah, daughter of Asher, is listed among Jacob's family who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Serah: A daughter of Asher and granddaughter of Jacob, one of the few women named in Israel's genealogies.

sentences: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob and founded the Zerahite clan.
Listed as Zohar, he went down to Egypt with Jacob among the sons of Simeon (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Zerah: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob and founded the Zerahite clan.

sentences: Matthan fathered Jacob, the father of Joseph the husband of Mary (Matthew 1).
links.card_of: Matthan: Son of Eleazar and grandfather of Joseph, Mary's husband, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

sentences: A son of Asher and grandson of Jacob, ancestor of the clan of the Imnites.
Imnah is listed first among the sons of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Imnah: A son of Asher and grandson of Jacob, ancestor of the clan of the Imnites.

sentences: Jacob and his whole family moved to Egypt and settled in Goshen (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Egypt: The great kingdom of the Nile valley, where Israel grew into a nation and was later enslaved.

sentences: Jacob crossed the Jordan with only his staff on his way to Haran (Genesis 32).
links.card_of: Jordan: The river flowing from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea, the eastern boundary of Canaan.

sentences: Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well (John 4).
links.card_of: Samaria: The capital of the northern kingdom of Israel, and later the hill region between Galilee and Judea.

sentences: Jacob and Laban made a covenant in the hill country of Gilead (Genesis 31).
links.card_of: Gilead: A fertile, hilly region east of the Jordan River, settled by Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.

sentences: Esau asked Jacob for the red stew, and so he was called Edom (Genesis 25).
Obadiah announced judgment on Edom for its violence against Jacob (Obadiah 1).
links.card_of: Edom: The land of Esau's descendants, south and southeast of the Dead Sea.

sentences: During a famine, Jacob sent his sons from Canaan to buy grain in Egypt (Genesis 42).
links.card_of: Canaan: The land between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean that God promised to Abraham's offspring.

sentences: A town north of Jerusalem where God met Jacob, later a center of idolatrous worship in Israel.
Jacob named it after God met him there in a dream of a stairway reaching to heaven (Genesis 28).
Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven and named the place Bethel (Genesis 28).
links.card_of: Bethel: A town north of Jerusalem where God met Jacob, later a center of idolatrous worship in Israel.

sentences: Jacob offered sacrifices at Beersheba on his way to Egypt (Genesis 46).
links.card_of: Beersheba: A town in the Negeb at the southern edge of Israel, linked with the patriarchs.

sentences: Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau in the land of Seir (Genesis 32).
After meeting Jacob, Esau returned to Seir (Genesis 33).
links.card_of: Seir: The mountainous land south of the Dead Sea where Esau's descendants, the Edomites, lived.

sentences: Jacob said Zebulun would dwell at the shore of the sea (Genesis 49).
links.card_of: Zebulun: The tribal territory of Zebulun in lower Galilee, between the Sea of Galilee and the Mediterranean.

sentences: Named for Benjamin; dying Rachel called him Ben-oni, but Jacob named him Benjamin (Genesis 35).
links.card_of: Benjamin: The tribal territory allotted to Benjamin, a narrow strip of hill country between Judah and Ephraim.

sentences: When angels of God met Jacob there, he said, This is God's camp, and named it Mahanaim (Genesis 32).
Jacob met the angels of God here and named the place Mahanaim (Genesis 32).
links.card_of: Mahanaim: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, near the Jabbok River.

sentences: A fertile region of Egypt where Jacob's family settled.
Joseph met his father Jacob in Goshen (Genesis 46).
Pharaoh granted Jacob's family the land of Goshen for their flocks (Genesis 47).
links.card_of: Goshen: A fertile region of Egypt where Jacob's family settled.

sentences: Rebekah sent Jacob to her brother Laban in Haran to escape Esau (Genesis 27).
Jacob met Rachel by a well near Haran (Genesis 29).
links.card_of: Haran: A city in upper Mesopotamia where Abraham's family settled and Laban lived.

sentences: Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan-aram to take a wife from Laban's daughters (Genesis 28).
Jacob left Paddan-aram with the livestock he had gained there (Genesis 31).
God appeared to Jacob again after he came from Paddan-aram and renamed him Israel (Genesis 35).
links.card_of: Paddan-aram: The region of upper Mesopotamia around Haran, home of Abraham's relatives.

sentences: Jacob built a house there and made booths for his livestock, so it was called Succoth (Genesis 33).
Jacob built a house and shelters for his livestock and named the place Succoth (Genesis 33).
links.card_of: Succoth: A town in the Jordan Valley east of the river, near the Jabbok.

sentences: Jacob crossed the ford of the Jabbok and wrestled with a man until daybreak (Genesis 32).
links.card_of: Jabbok: A river flowing west into the Jordan, forming a natural boundary in the land of Gilead.

sentences: Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Kiriath-arba, where Isaac died (Genesis 35).
links.card_of: Kiriath-arba: The older name of Hebron, a city in the hill country of Judah named after Arba of the Anakim.

sentences: After his dream, Jacob renamed the city of Luz Bethel (Genesis 28).

Jacob told Joseph that God Almighty appeared to him at Luz (Genesis 48).
links.card_of: Luz: The original Canaanite name of Bethel, a town north of Jerusalem.

sentences: Jacob asked to be buried there with Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, and Leah (Genesis 49).
Jacob's sons carried his body from Egypt and buried him at Machpelah (Genesis 50).
links.card_of: Machpelah: A field and cave near Mamre that Abraham bought as a family burial place.

sentences: Jacob came home to Isaac at Mamre, where Isaac died (Genesis 35).
Jacob was buried in the field east of Mamre (Genesis 50).
links.card_of: Mamre: A place near Hebron where Abraham lived, facing the cave of Machpelah.

sentences: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, named for the watchpost set up by Jacob and Laban.
Jacob and Laban made a covenant heap called Mizpah as a witness between them (Genesis 31).
links.card_of: Mizpah: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, named for the watchpost set up by Jacob and Laban.

sentences: Hosea recalled that Jacob fled to the land of Aram (Hosea 12).
links.card_of: Aram: The land of the Arameans north and northeast of Israel, centered on Damascus.

sentences: A place by the Jabbok where Jacob saw God face to face, later a fortified town.

Jacob named the place Peniel, saying he had seen God face to face (Genesis 32).
links.card_of: Penuel: A place by the Jabbok where Jacob saw God face to face, later a fortified town.

sentences: Jacob tells Joseph he buried Rachel on the way to Ephrath (Genesis 48).
links.card_of: Ephrath: An older name for Bethlehem in Judah, near where Rachel died and was buried.

sentences: Jacob named it after God met him there in a dream of a stairway reaching to heaven (Genesis 28).

links.card_of: Bethel: A Canaanite royal city north of Jerusalem, near Ai, conquered by Joshua.

options.who: A man in Uzziah's day who instructed the king in the fear of God.

options.name: Zechariah
options.who: A prophet after the exile, son of Berechiah and grandson of Iddo, who urged rebuilding the temple.

options.name: Zechariah
options.who: A family head of the descendants of Parosh who returned from Babylon with Ezra.

options.name: Zechariah
options.who: The son of Bebai, a family head who returned from Babylon with Ezra.

options.name: Zechariah
options.who: One of the leaders Ezra sent to recruit Levites for the journey from Babylon to Jerusalem.

options.name: Zechariah
options.who: A descendant of Elam who had married a foreign wife after the return from exile.

sentences: Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah reign in Israel.
Joash repairs the temple while Jehoiada lives, but afterward turns to idols, has Zechariah stoned, and is assassinated.
Jehoiada's son Zechariah warns them and is stoned in the temple court at the king's command.
He seeks God in the days of Zechariah, who instructs him in the fear of God.
Encouraged by Haggai and Zechariah, they finish the temple under Darius and celebrate Passover.
Prompted by Haggai and Zechariah, the Jews resume building, and the governor Tattenai writes to Darius about it.
Zechariah encourages the returned exiles through visions and oracles about rebuilding the temple and God's coming king and kingdom.
Zechariah begins prophesying in Darius's second year with a call to return to the LORD.
Zechariah calls the people to return to the LORD and sees visions of horsemen and of four horns and craftsmen.
Zechariah sees a golden lampstand and two olive trees, and learns that Zerubbabel will finish the temple by God's Spirit.
Zechariah sees a flying scroll of curses and a woman in a basket representing wickedness carried away to Shinar.
Zechariah sees four chariots patrolling the earth, then crowns Joshua as a sign of the Branch who will build the temple.
Zechariah acts as a shepherd for a flock doomed to slaughter, is rejected and paid thirty shekels, and breaks his staffs.
Zechariah doubts Gabriel's message and is struck mute, while Mary accepts the news humbly.
Mary visits Elizabeth and praises God, and Zechariah prophesies at John's birth.
Prophet, son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, who prepared the way for Jesus and baptized him.
The angel told Zechariah to call him John; when relatives objected, Zechariah wrote, 'His name is John' (Luke 1).
An angel announced his birth to his father Zechariah in the temple (Luke 1).
links.card_of: John the Baptist: Prophet, son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, who prepared the way for Jesus and baptized him.

sentences: Urged by Haggai and Zechariah, he resumed work on the temple (Ezra 5; Haggai 1).
links.card_of: Zerubbabel: A descendant of David and governor of Judah who led exiles home and rebuilt the temple.

sentences: In Zechariah's vision his filthy garments were replaced with clean ones (Zechariah 3).
Zechariah was told to set a crown on his head as a sign (Zechariah 6).
links.card_of: Joshua: High priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and helped lead the rebuilding of the temple.

sentences: After Jehoiada died, he served idols and had Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned (2 Chronicles 24).
links.card_of: Joash: King of Judah, rescued as an infant, who repaired the temple but later turned from the LORD.

sentences: His son Zechariah succeeded him and reigned six months (2 Kings 15).
links.card_of: Jeroboam: King of Israel, son of Joash, who restored Israel's borders; often called Jeroboam II.

sentences: Zechariah set a crown on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak (Zechariah 6).
links.card_of: Jehozadak: A priest, son of Seraiah, taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar and father of Joshua the high priest.

sentences: He and Zechariah prophesied to the Jews, and the rebuilding of the temple resumed (Ezra 5).
links.card_of: Haggai: A prophet to the returned exiles who urged them to finish rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem.

sentences: Zechariah served as a priest in the days of Herod, king of Judea (Luke 1).
links.card_of: Herod: King of Judea when Jesus was born, who tried to kill the child Jesus.

sentences: Wife of the priest Zechariah and relative of Mary, who bore John the Baptist in old age.
links.card_of: Elizabeth: Wife of the priest Zechariah and relative of Mary, who bore John the Baptist in old age.

sentences: His son Zechariah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting (1 Chronicles 9).
links.card_of: Meshelemiah: A Korahite Levite, son of Kore, who headed a family of gatekeepers in David's time.

sentences: Zechariah foresees the family of the house of Nathan mourning by itself (Zechariah 12).
links.card_of: Nathan: A son of David and Bathsheba, born in Jerusalem, through whom Luke traces Jesus' genealogy.

sentences: A priest of David's time whose family formed the eighth priestly division, to which Zechariah later belonged.
Centuries later, Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, served as a priest of the division of Abijah (Luke 1).
links.card_of: Abijah: A priest of David's time whose family formed the eighth priestly division, to which Zechariah later belonged.

sentences: The son of Iddo and father of the post-exilic prophet Zechariah.
The word of the LORD came to his son Zechariah in Darius's second year (Zechariah 1).
Ezra calls Zechariah the son of Iddo, naming his grandfather (Ezra 5).
links.card_of: Berechiah: The son of Iddo and father of the post-exilic prophet Zechariah.

sentences: An angel who stands in God's presence and was sent with messages to Daniel, Zechariah, and Mary.
He announced John's birth to Zechariah and made him unable to speak for not believing (Luke 1).
links.card_of: Gabriel: An angel who stands in God's presence and was sent with messages to Daniel, Zechariah, and Mary.

sentences: A priest who returned from exile, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah.
Ezra calls the prophet Zechariah his son, naming him by his grandfather (Ezra 5).
Through the preaching of Zechariah the son of Iddo, the elders finished building the temple (Ezra 6).
links.card_of: Iddo: A priest who returned from exile, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah.

sentences: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against King Zechariah of Israel, killed him, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
Zechariah's death fulfilled the LORD's word that Jehu's dynasty would last four generations (2 Kings 15).
links.card_of: Shallum: A king of Israel who seized the throne by assassination and reigned only one month.

sentences: Zechariah of the descendants of Parosh was registered with 150 men in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
links.card_of: Zechariah: A family head of the descendants of Parosh who returned from Babylon with Ezra.

sentences: Zechariah son of Bebai was registered with 28 men in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
links.card_of: Zechariah: The son of Bebai, a family head who returned from Babylon with Ezra.

sentences: Finding no Levites in the camp at the Ahava canal, Ezra summoned Zechariah and other leaders (Ezra 8).
links.card_of: Zechariah: One of the leaders Ezra sent to recruit Levites for the journey from Babylon to Jerusalem.

sentences: The father, or family head, of Zechariah, who led twenty-eight men back from Babylon with Ezra.
Zechariah son of Bebai returned from Babylon to Jerusalem in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
links.card_of: Bebai: The father, or family head, of Zechariah, who led twenty-eight men back from Babylon with Ezra.

sentences: The father of Shallum, who killed King Zechariah of Israel and reigned one month.
Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against King Zechariah, killed him, and reigned in his place (2 Kings 15).
links.card_of: Jabesh: The father of Shallum, who killed King Zechariah of Israel and reigned one month.

sentences: Zechariah of the sons of Parosh was registered with 150 men in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
links.card_of: Parosh: An ancestor whose descendants formed a large family among the exiles who returned from Babylon.

sentences: Zechariah foresaw the land from Geba to Rimmon becoming a plain (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Geba: A Levitical town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, often marking the northern edge of Judah.

sentences: Zechariah foresaw the Lord standing on the Mount of Olives as it splits in two (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Mount of Olives: A ridge east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley.

sentences: Zechariah foresaw the coming king ruling from the River to the ends of the earth (Zechariah 9).
links.card_of: Euphrates River: The Euphrates, often called simply the River, the great river of Mesopotamia.

sentences: Zechariah saw wickedness carried in a basket to Shinar (Zechariah 5).
links.card_of: Shinar: The ancient name for the plain of southern Mesopotamia, where Babylon stood.

sentences: Zechariah described Jerusalem secure from the Corner Gate onward (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Corner Gate: A gate at the northwest corner of Jerusalem's city wall.

sentences: Zechariah foresees Jerusalem restored from the Benjamin Gate to the Corner Gate (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Benjamin Gate: A gate on the north side of Jerusalem facing the territory of Benjamin.

sentences: Zechariah foresees the land leveled from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Rimmon: A town in the far south of Judah, later allotted to Simeon.

sentences: Zechariah foresees Jerusalem inhabited from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Tower of Hananel: A tower on the northern wall of Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate.

sentences: A region in Syria named first in Zechariah's oracle of judgment on Israel's northern neighbors.
links.card_of: Hadrach: A region in Syria named first in Zechariah's oracle of judgment on Israel's northern neighbors.

sentences: Zechariah foresaw the Lord standing on the Mount of Olives as it splits in two (Zechariah 14).
links.card_of: Mount of Olives: A ridge east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley.

options.name: Zerah
options.who: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob and founded the Zerahite clan.

options.name: Zohar
options.who: A Hittite, father of Ephron, who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah.

sentences: A Hittite, son of Zohar, who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah as a family tomb.
links.card_of: Ephron: A Hittite, son of Zohar, who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah as a family tomb.

options.name: Euphrates

options.who: The Euphrates, often called simply the River, the great river of Mesopotamia.

sentences: The Euphrates, often called simply the River, the great river of Mesopotamia.
God promised Israel territory reaching to the River (Deuteronomy 11).
